report_metadata.sdlc_rationale: Regulatory compliance requirements (21 CFR Part 11, ICH E6(R2), EMA Annex 11) are fully defined and non-negotiable; technology stack is mandated (Medidata Rave integration, CDISC standards); deadline is fixed at 12 months with no flexibility. However, team composition is explicitly TBD, creating execution uncertainty that would normally push toward Hybrid — but the regulatory framework and integration contracts are sufficiently concrete to support Predictive planning with explicit staffing assumptions.

project_understanding.primary_goal: Build a clinical trial data management system that integrates with Medidata Rave EDC, generates CDISC-compliant datasets for regulatory submission, and implements safety signal detection with Bayesian adaptive design, all in compliance with FDA 21 CFR Part 11, ICH E6(R2), and EMA Annex 11.
project_understanding.beneficiary: Clinical operations team, biostatistics team, regulatory affairs division
project_understanding.trigger: Pharmaceutical research division requires FDA-compliant data management infrastructure for Phase II and Phase III trials to support NDA submissions.
success_definition: System passes FDA 21 CFR Part 11 audit and achieves compliance certification
Medidata Rave integration tested and validated with real trial data
CDISC SDTM and ADaM datasets generated and accepted by regulatory affairs for NDA submission
Blinded randomisation with IWRS integration operational and validated
Real-time safety signal detection algorithm deployed and validated against historical trial data
Clinical operations team trained and system in production use within 12 months
supporting_quotes: Build a clinical trial data management system for our pharmaceutical research division
must handle Phase II and Phase III trial data in compliance with 21 CFR Part 11 (FDA electronic records), ICH E6(R2) GCP guidelines, and EMA Annex 11
integrate with our existing EDC system (Medidata Rave)
generate CDISC SDTM and ADaM datasets for NDA submission
support blinded randomisation with IWRS integration
provide real-time safety signal detection using Bayesian adaptive design thresholds
Timeline: 12 months. Budget: $2.4 million. Team: To be determined

assumption_log.what: Medidata Rave API documentation, sandbox environment, and integration support are available and accessible to the development team within Phase 1.
assumption_log.why: External API integration is a critical path dependency. Without confirmed sandbox access and documented contracts, Phase 2 development cannot begin. This is a standard prerequisite for TYPE_D projects.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 11.2 — Risk identification before planning baseline; Section 9.2 — Resource estimation tied to external dependencies.
assumption_log.consequence: Development blocked for 4-8 weeks while API access is negotiated. Critical path extends beyond 12-month deadline.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows Phase 2 to start on schedule. Risks: if Medidata support is slow or API contracts are unclear, entire integration timeline slips.

assumption_log.what: CDISC SDTM and ADaM dataset generation requirements are fully defined by regulatory affairs and documented in a specification before Phase 2 development begins.
assumption_log.why: CDISC compliance is non-negotiable for FDA submission. Vague or evolving dataset requirements will cause rework in Phase 4 (QA) or post-launch. This must be locked in Phase 1.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 5.4 — Scope baseline requires accepted requirements; Section 13.2 — Stakeholder requirements documented before execution.
assumption_log.consequence: Dataset generation logic must be rewritten in Phase 4, delaying UAT and regulatory review. NDA submission timeline at risk.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: prevents rework and regulatory rejection. Risks: if regulatory affairs cannot finalize specs in Phase 1, project enters Adaptive mode and timeline extends.

assumption_log.what: 21 CFR Part 11 compliance scope is limited to electronic records and audit trails within the system; FDA pre-submission meeting (Type B or Type C) is NOT required before Phase 2 development.
assumption_log.why: 21 CFR Part 11 is a well-established regulatory standard with known implementation patterns (audit logging, digital signatures, access controls). Assuming no pre-submission meeting allows Phase 2 to proceed in parallel with regulatory review. If a pre-submission meeting is required, Phase 1 extends by 8-12 weeks.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 11.2 — Risk identification; Section 6.4 — Schedule baseline derived from scope definition.
assumption_log.consequence: If FDA pre-submission meeting is mandatory, Phase 1 extends 8-12 weeks, compressing Phase 2-4 or pushing deadline past 12 months.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows Phase 2 to start on schedule. Risks: if regulatory affairs requires pre-submission meeting, critical path extends and budget may increase for extended team allocation.

assumption_log.what: Bayesian adaptive design thresholds for safety signal detection are defined by biostatistics team and provided as a specification document (not to be designed by the development team) before Phase 2 begins.
assumption_log.why: Safety signal detection is a specialized biostatistical domain. Assuming the algorithm is specified (not invented) by the project team prevents scope creep and rework. If the development team must design the algorithm, Phase 2 extends significantly and requires biostatistician on critical path.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 5.4 — Scope baseline; Section 9.2 — Resource estimation tied to WBS.
assumption_log.consequence: If algorithm design is in scope, Phase 2 extends 6-8 weeks and requires full-time biostatistician (not available). Critical path slips.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: limits scope to implementation, not research. Risks: if biostatistics team cannot finalize algorithm spec, project enters Adaptive mode.

assumption_log.what: IWRS (Interactive Web Response System) integration is with a third-party vendor (e.g., Parexel, Covance) whose API is documented and sandbox-accessible; the vendor is contractually obligated to support integration within the project timeline.
assumption_log.why: IWRS is a specialized randomisation service. Assuming vendor support and API availability prevents Phase 3 integration testing from being blocked. If IWRS vendor is uncooperative or API is undocumented, Phase 3 extends significantly.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 11.2 — Risk identification; Section 9.2 — External dependency estimation.
assumption_log.consequence: If IWRS vendor does not provide API documentation or sandbox, Phase 3 integration testing is blocked for 4-6 weeks. Critical path slips.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows Phase 3 integration to proceed on schedule. Risks: if IWRS vendor is slow or uncooperative, timeline extends.

assumption_log.what: The development team has or will hire expertise in 21 CFR Part 11 compliance, CDISC standards, and clinical trial data management; no external regulatory consulting is required beyond Phase 1 review.
assumption_log.why: Clinical trial software is a specialized domain. Assuming in-house expertise (or hiring it) prevents dependency on expensive external consultants. If the team lacks this expertise and must hire consultants for Phases 2-4, budget increases and critical path extends.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 9.2 — Resource estimation; Section 11.2 — Risk identification for skill gaps.
assumption_log.consequence: If team lacks clinical trial expertise, external consultants required for Phases 2-4 at $150-250/hour. Budget increases by $200k-400k and critical path extends due to knowledge transfer delays.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: keeps budget within $2.4M and timeline within 12 months. Risks: if team is hired without clinical trial experience, rework and delays are likely.

risk_register.description: If 21 CFR Part 11 compliance scope is not fully defined in Phase 1 or if FDA pre-submission meeting is required but not scheduled, then Phase 1 extends 8-12 weeks and critical path slips past 12-month deadline.
risk_register.trigger: Regulatory affairs indicates pre-submission meeting is required; Phase 1 requirements document does not include detailed 21 CFR Part 11 implementation plan.
risk_register.mitigation: Schedule regulatory requirements workshop in Week 1 of Phase 1; confirm with regulatory affairs whether FDA pre-submission meeting is required before Phase 2 begins; document all compliance requirements in writing.
risk_register.contingency: If pre-submission meeting is required, extend Phase 1 by 8-12 weeks and compress Phase 2-4 or extend overall timeline past 12 months. Escalate to executive sponsor for timeline re-approval.

risk_register.description: If Medidata Rave API documentation is incomplete, sandbox environment is not accessible, or integration support is unavailable, then Phase 2 development is blocked for 4-8 weeks.
risk_register.trigger: Medidata sandbox access not confirmed by end of Week 2 of Phase 1; API documentation incomplete or unclear.
risk_register.mitigation: Confirm Medidata Rave API access and sandbox environment in Week 1 of Phase 1; establish integration support SLA with Medidata; obtain test data for Phase 2 development.
risk_register.contingency: If Medidata support is slow, engage Medidata professional services for expedited integration support. Budget additional $50k-100k for professional services.

risk_register.description: If CDISC SDTM and ADaM dataset specifications are not finalized by biostatistics team before Phase 2 begins, then dataset generation logic must be rewritten in Phase 4, delaying UAT and regulatory review.
risk_register.trigger: Biostatistics team cannot provide CDISC specification by end of Phase 1; specification is vague or incomplete.
risk_register.mitigation: Schedule CDISC specification workshop with biostatistics in Week 1 of Phase 1; obtain written specification by end of Week 4 of Phase 1; have regulatory affairs review specification for completeness.
risk_register.contingency: If specification is delayed, Phase 2 development proceeds with assumed CDISC structure; Phase 4 includes rework time for dataset generation logic. Timeline extends by 2-4 weeks.

risk_register.description: If the development team lacks expertise in 21 CFR Part 11 compliance, CDISC standards, and clinical trial data management, then external regulatory consultants are required for Phases 2-4, increasing budget by $200k-400k and extending timeline by 4-6 weeks.
risk_register.trigger: Development team does not have prior experience with clinical trial software; team members are unfamiliar with 21 CFR Part 11 or CDISC standards.
risk_register.mitigation: Hire or allocate Clinical Trial Compliance Lead with 5+ years of 21 CFR Part 11 experience before Phase 1 begins. Conduct knowledge transfer sessions in Phase 1 to upskill development team.
risk_register.contingency: If team lacks expertise, engage external regulatory consultants for Phases 2-4 at $150-250/hour. Budget additional $200k-400k and extend timeline by 4-6 weeks.

risk_register.description: If IWRS (Interactive Web Response System) vendor does not provide API documentation, sandbox access, or integration support, then Phase 3 integration testing is blocked for 4-6 weeks.
risk_register.trigger: IWRS vendor API documentation not received by end of Phase 1; sandbox access not confirmed; vendor support SLA not signed.
risk_register.mitigation: Confirm IWRS vendor integration contract and API documentation in Week 2 of Phase 1; establish integration support SLA; obtain sandbox access before Phase 2 begins.
risk_register.contingency: If IWRS vendor is uncooperative, engage IWRS professional services or consider alternative randomisation system. Timeline extends by 4-6 weeks.

risk_register.description: If Bayesian adaptive design algorithm specification is not provided by biostatistics team before Phase 2 begins, then development team must design the algorithm, extending Phase 2 by 6-8 weeks and requiring full-time biostatistician on critical path.
risk_register.trigger: Biostatistics team cannot provide algorithm specification by end of Phase 1; specification is vague or incomplete.
risk_register.mitigation: Schedule algorithm specification workshop with biostatistics in Week 1 of Phase 1; obtain written specification with safety signal thresholds and validation criteria by end of Week 4 of Phase 1.
risk_register.contingency: If specification is delayed, Phase 2 development proceeds with assumed algorithm structure; Phase 3 includes algorithm refinement. Timeline extends by 2-4 weeks.

risk_register.description: If any critical path task (Medidata integration, CDISC dataset generation, Bayesian algorithm integration, compliance review) slips by more than 1 week, then overall project timeline extends past 12-month deadline.
risk_register.trigger: Critical path task completion date slips by more than 1 week; critical path duration exceeds 220 days.
risk_register.mitigation: Allocate critical path roles (Medidata Integration Lead, Data Engineer, Biostatistics Engineer, Clinical Trial Compliance Lead) at 100% full-time. Establish weekly critical path status reviews. Identify and mitigate risks early.
risk_register.contingency: If critical path slips, compress Phase 4 (QA & Testing) or extend overall timeline past 12 months. Escalate to executive sponsor for timeline re-approval.

risk_register.description: If any critical path role (Medidata Integration Lead, Data Engineer, Biostatistics Engineer, Clinical Trial Compliance Lead) is allocated part-time or shared with other projects, then critical path extends and 12-month deadline is at risk.
risk_register.trigger: Critical path role allocated less than 80% to this project; role shared with competing project or priority.
risk_register.mitigation: Confirm full-time allocation (80-100%) for all critical path roles before Phase 1 begins. Obtain written commitment from resource managers. Establish escalation path for resource conflicts.
risk_register.contingency: If critical path role is pulled to another project, hire contractor or backfill with internal resource. Budget additional $50k-150k for contractor.

risk_register.description: If security review or penetration testing identifies critical vulnerabilities in Phase 3, then Phase 4 (QA & Testing) extends by 2-4 weeks to remediate and re-test.
risk_register.trigger: Security review or penetration testing identifies critical or high-severity vulnerabilities; remediation requires code changes.
risk_register.mitigation: Conduct security design review in Phase 1; implement security best practices in Phase 2 development; conduct security review early in Phase 3 to identify issues before Phase 4.
risk_register.contingency: If critical vulnerabilities are found, allocate additional development time in Phase 4 for remediation and re-testing. Timeline extends by 1-2 weeks.

risk_register.description: If CDISC dataset generation logic is complex or requires significant rework to match regulatory requirements, then Phase 3 and Phase 4 extend by 2-4 weeks.
risk_register.trigger: CDISC dataset generation logic fails validation in Phase 3; output does not match specification; regulatory affairs requests changes.
risk_register.mitigation: Obtain detailed CDISC specification from biostatistics in Phase 1; validate dataset generation logic against test data in Phase 2; conduct early validation in Phase 3.
risk_register.contingency: If dataset generation logic requires rework, allocate additional development time in Phase 3 and Phase 4. Timeline extends by 1-2 weeks.

risk_register.description: If Medidata Rave API integration encounters unexpected data schema issues or API behavior changes, then Phase 2 development extends by 2-4 weeks.
risk_register.trigger: Medidata API returns unexpected data format; API behavior differs from documentation; schema changes between sandbox and production.
risk_register.mitigation: Conduct thorough API testing in Medidata sandbox in Phase 2; document all API quirks and edge cases; establish communication channel with Medidata support for rapid issue resolution.
risk_register.contingency: If API issues are encountered, allocate additional development time in Phase 2 for troubleshooting and workarounds. Timeline extends by 1-2 weeks.

scoping_options.description: Reduce Phase II and Phase III trial scope to Phase II only in MVP; defer Phase III support to Phase 2 release (6 months post-launch).

scoping_options.tradeoffs: Phase III trial support deferred; regulatory affairs may require Phase III support in MVP for NDA submission readiness. Requires stakeholder re-approval.

scoping_options.description: Defer real-time safety signal detection (Bayesian algorithm) to Phase 2 release; MVP includes data ingestion, CDISC dataset generation, and blinded randomisation only.
scoping_options.impact: Eliminates algorithm integration and validation from critical path; Phase 2 development compresses by 3-4 weeks; critical path reduces to ~190 days (27.1 weeks).
scoping_options.tradeoffs: Safety signal detection not available at launch; biostatistics team may require this feature for Phase II trial monitoring. Requires stakeholder re-approval.

scoping_options.description: Extend timeline to 15 months (39 weeks) to accommodate CRITICAL risks and provide schedule buffer; maintain full scope (Phase II and Phase III, CDISC SDTM and ADaM, Bayesian algorithm, IWRS integration).
scoping_options.impact: Provides 8-week buffer for risk mitigation; reduces schedule pressure on critical path roles; allows time for FDA pre-submission meeting if required.
scoping_options.tradeoffs: Misses 12-month deadline; requires stakeholder re-approval and budget adjustment for extended team allocation (~$300k additional cost for 3-month extension).
